name: Comeback Kid
label: Victory
lede: Two guitarists from a Winnipeg Christian hardcore band started a side project named after a Mario Lemieux headline, then one of them walked up to the microphone and never gave it back.

eras.title: A side project named for a hockey comeback
eras.text: Andrew Neufeld and Jeremy Hiebert were playing guitar in the Winnipeg band Figure Four when they started Comeback Kid on the side in 2001. They took the name from a newspaper headline about Mario Lemieux returning to the NHL, and within two years the side project had an album out.

years.h: Two guitarists from Figure Four start Comeback Kid in Winnipeg
years.p: Andrew Neufeld and Jeremy Hiebert of Figure Four form the band with singer Scott Wade and drummer Kyle Profeta. The name comes from a headline about Mario Lemieux coming back to the NHL.
years.xp:
Comeback Kid began in March 2001 as a side project for Neufeld and Hiebert, who were still in the Christian hardcore band Figure Four. Neufeld and Hiebert played guitar; Wade sang.

Wikipedia credits the name to a newspaper headline about Lemieux, the Pittsburgh Penguins star who came out of retirement in December 2000.

years.h: A six-song demo gets Comeback Kid out of Winnipeg
years.p: Comeback Kid's first recording is a six-song demo released in January 2002.

years.h: Comeback Kid signs to Facedown Records
years.p: The California label Facedown Records signs Comeback Kid in August 2002, and the band cuts its first album in November.

years.h: Turn It Around: 13 songs in 28 minutes on Facedown
years.p: Comeback Kid's debut, recorded November 2002, runs 28 minutes with Scott Wade singing and Cliff Heide on bass. Give Me Strength presses the vinyl. After it, the band tours full time.

eras.title: Thirteen days at the Blasting Room
eras.text: Comeback Kid went to Fort Collins, Colorado to make its second album with Bill Stevenson of the Descendents. Wake the Dead came out on Victory Records and turned a Winnipeg side project into a band hardcore kids sing back at every show.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wake the Dead · Wikipedia: Comeback Kid
years.h: Wake the Dead: 25 minutes cut with [[Bill Stevenson|328e3ae5-7d8c-4a01-b2b3-b8f41fb7bb23]]
years.p: Comeback Kid's second album was recorded in 13 days at the Blasting Room in Fort Collins, produced by Bill Stevenson and Jason Livermore. It reaches No. 16 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
years.xp:
The album's 11 songs run 25 minutes, 46 seconds. [[Russ Rankin|99fd5943-758d-4c1b-bd2c-4b6d0d1e037a]] of [[Good Riddance|ab4725b8-7a2f-429a-a55a-3dde07c9acea]] and Luke Friesen sing guests. It was Scott Wade's last album as the band's singer.

Wikipedia's album page lists Smallman as the label (catalog SMR 026); Wikipedia's band page credits Victory Records.

years.h: The song Wake the Dead lands in the video game Burnout Revenge
years.p: The title track of Wake the Dead goes on the soundtracks of EA's racing games Burnout Revenge and Burnout Legends.

eras.title: The guitarist takes the microphone
eras.text: When Scott Wade left, Comeback Kid did not hold auditions: guitarist Andrew Neufeld became the singer. Broadcasting... proved the swap worked, and the band spent the next two years on the road across North America and Europe.

years.src: Wikipedia: Comeback Kid · Wikipedia: Die Knowing · Wikipedia: A Shipwreck in the Sand
years.h: Scott Wade quits Comeback Kid. Guitarist Andrew Neufeld starts singing
years.p: After Wake the Dead, singer Scott Wade leaves Comeback Kid and co-founder Andrew Neufeld moves from rhythm guitar to lead vocals.
years.xp: Wade stayed friendly with the band: he sings guest vocals on the song Full Swing on Die Knowing in 2014, and on [[Silverstein|d89de379-665d-425c-b2e9-41b95d1edb36]]'s A Shipwreck in the Sand in 2009.

years.h: Broadcasting...: Andrew Neufeld's first album as singer
years.p: Back at the Blasting Room with Bill Stevenson in November 2006, Comeback Kid makes a record that reaches No. 3 on Heatseekers and No. 129 on the Billboard 200. The title track ends up in NHL 2K8.

years.h: Comeback Kid tours with [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]] and on Never Say Die
years.p: Comeback Kid tours North America with Rise Against and Europe on the Never Say Die tour with [[Parkway Drive|a436dd02-0549-4c91-b608-df451217fdeb]], then takes a short break at the end of 2007.

years.h: Bassist Kevin Call leaves Comeback Kid on good terms
years.p: Kevin Call, the bassist on Wake the Dead and Broadcasting..., leaves and Matt Keil takes over bass.

years.h: Through the Noise: six years on a CD and DVD
years.p: Comeback Kid's first live release documents the band's first six years, with a live set recorded in Leipzig, Germany in fall 2007.

eras.title: Distort, Victory, and a new drummer
eras.text: With Smallman gone, Comeback Kid moved to Distort in Canada and stayed with Victory Records for the US. Two more albums came out on Victory before the band's founding drummer left to cook in South Africa.

years.h: Symptoms + Cures: Distort in Canada, Victory in the US
years.p: Comeback Kid's fourth album is made in Toronto with producers Eric Ratz and Kenny Luong. Members of [[Cancer Bats|00b952be-6c97-4880-84f9-06de584b491b]], [[A Wilhelm Scream|657ec972-3ab1-48a8-b472-1f1c210aaf17]] and Architects guest.

years.h: A van crash with Gravemaker becomes the song G.M. Vincent and I
years.p: Andrew Neufeld was in a van accident with the band Gravemaker. According to Wikipedia, it inspired the Comeback Kid song G.M. Vincent and I.

years.h: Casey Hjelmberg leaves. Stu Ross of [[Misery Signals|0b0b523f-e9d5-4f18-919c-ebf084a58c26]] joins
years.p: Guitarist Casey Hjelmberg announces he's leaving Comeback Kid. Stu Ross, from Misery Signals and Living with Lions, replaces him.

years.h: Die Knowing: the last Comeback Kid album on Victory
years.p: Produced by Kyle Black, led by the single Should Know Better. Original singer Scott Wade comes back to guest on Full Swing.

years.h: Founding drummer Kyle Profeta quits to cook in South Africa
years.p: Kyle Profeta, Comeback Kid's drummer since 2001, leaves to focus on his culinary skills in South Africa.

eras.title: Twenty years of Wake the Dead
eras.text: Comeback Kid moved to Nuclear Blast and kept making records, but the song fans wait for is still one from 2005. In 2025 the band toured Wake the Dead in full and lost a former bassist to ALS.

years.h: Outsider: Comeback Kid's first album on Nuclear Blast
years.p: Comeback Kid's sixth album is its first after Victory Records, released worldwide by the metal label Nuclear Blast.

years.h: Heavy Steps, on New Damage and Nuclear Blast
years.p: Comeback Kid's seventh album comes out on New Damage in Canada and Nuclear Blast everywhere else.

years.h: The Trouble EP, on SharpTone
years.p: Comeback Kid releases the Trouble EP through SharpTone Records.

years.cap: The Wake the Dead 20th anniversary tour
q: the biggest moment in every single set that we've played
years.src: Wikipedia: Wake the Dead · Wikipedia: Comeback Kid
years.h: Comeback Kid plays Wake the Dead in full for its 20th
years.p: Comeback Kid tours the US, then Canada in September, playing Wake the Dead start to finish, and re-records the title track.
years.xp: Andrew Neufeld said the song Wake the Dead lands hardest in every set the band plays, from Asia and South America to Europe, Africa and North America. The band re-recorded it for the anniversary.

years.h: Former bassist Matt Keil dies of ALS
years.p: Matt Keil, Comeback Kid's bassist from late 2007 and on Die Knowing, died in July 2025 from ALS, according to Wikipedia.
